question: Should OpenClaw publish official standalone Android APKs outside Google Play, and if so which signed flavor, release channel, provenance, and security process owns that distribution?
rationale: Current code can build a signed third-party APK locally, but making it an official GitHub or F-Droid asset changes release trust, sideload guidance, signing custody, and support expectations.

options.title: Approve signed standalone APK releases
options.body: Reuse or harden the existing third-party APK archive path, publish checksums/provenance with release assets, and update Android docs for non-Play installs.

options.title: Stay Google Play-only
options.body: Keep official distribution on Google Play and update docs to state that standalone APKs are not currently published or supported.

options.title: Prefer F-Droid or vetted channel first
options.body: Investigate F-Droid or another vetted channel before GitHub APK assets, with the same signing and provenance requirements.

recommendation.title: Approve signed standalone APK releases
recommendation.body: Reuse or harden the existing third-party APK archive path, publish checksums/provenance with release assets, and update Android docs for non-Play installs.

likelyOwner.reason: The current Android app, docs, and release-surface history point to steipete, and the choice spans Android product direction plus release trust.
